correctness.rationale: A has order 10 modulo 11, and A^10=I+11C with C nonzero modulo 11. Odd-prime binomial lifting raises the first nonzero congruence valuation by one at each step, and returning the initial consecutive Fibonacci pair is equivalent to A returning to the identity. For the ten index branches, the reduced divided difference of the Fibonacci interpolation is 8Lᵢ; only i=5 is singular. Each other branch is an isometry after scaling by 11 and hits each target in its residue disk once. At i=5, the chosen root satisfies s≡73 modulo 121 and ℓ/11≡6 modulo 11; Binet gives κ cosh((1+2t)ℓ). The square root used to normalize κ(ℓ/11)^2/4 exists as that expression is 1 modulo 11. The higher coefficients of the normalized sinh factor are in 121 Z₁₁, so the normalized V has unit divided difference 2u modulo 11. Thus F=κ+242V² with V bijective at each finite precision. There are 11 lifts of each root from precision k−2 to index precision k−1; k=2 uses the trivial ring, and k=1 is the direct ten-term count. The valuation split of the squares gives the stated root counts, central fiber sizes, and support and density. An independent exact replay checked every target at the sampled levels 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 and first-return states through the asserted periods; it is finite corroboration, not the all-level proof.
residual_risks: The replay has finite exponent coverage; the unbounded conclusion uses the exact lifting and isometry proof.

evidence: The distinct composite record gives (E₁₁,b,O₁₁,b) as even and odd counts over the least local period, including the divisible-square-root count for 5z²−4 when z≡5 modulo 11.

On that target class, 5z²−4=5(z−κ)(z+κ), with 5(z+κ) a unit. For z≡κ modulo 121 set δ=(z−κ)/121; the ratio of the discriminant's scaled factor to the frozen root coefficient δ/2 is the square unit 10(z+κ)≡1 modulo 11, interpreted as a multiplier also at δ=0.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The divisible roots are u=11v; dividing their congruence by 121 and rescaling v by a square-root unit yields exactly 11R_(b−2)(δ/2) for b≥2. If z is outside that disk but in the singular target class there is no divisible root; at b=1 exactly one root remains. The two formulations agree at every precision and every target, not just on their support.
